title: Relate $$x$$ and $$\theta$$
text: To find the period of $$\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4}x\right), $$ determine the values of $$x$$ for which the argument $$\frac{\pi}{4}x$$ spans from $$0$$ to $$\pi, $$ since $$\tan(\theta)$$ completes one full period over that interval.

title: Substitute
text: Substitute $$\theta$$ with $$\frac{\pi x}{4}$$ in the interval for a single period ( $$0<\theta<\pi$$ ): \n $$0<\frac{\pi x}{4}<\pi$$.

title: Solve for the interval of $$x$$
text: Dividing the entire inequality 0< $$\frac{\pi{x}}{4}$$ < $$\pi$$ by $$\frac{\pi}{4}$$, we get $$0<x<\operatorname{\pi}\left(\frac{4}{\pi}\right)=4$$. Thus, the period is $$4$$.
